answer: A farm running 138 keys hence pays for 138 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the sable declaration. Because the zenith audit recomputes usage from the river history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 183 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
